ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (CMF), Articles L.561-1 et seq. and R.561-1 et seq. (AML/CFT obligations for obliged entities, customer due diligence and PEP measures); CMF Articles L.561-45 to L.561-57 and R.561-57-1 et seq. (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs – RBE); Loi n° 2016-1691 of 9 December 2016 (Sapin II) establishing the UBO register; Décret n° 2020-115 of 12 February 2020 (UBO declaration modalities and access rules); Directive (EU) 2015/849 (AMLD4) as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/843 (AMLD5); Regulation (EU) 2015/847 and Regulation (EU) 2023/1113 (information accompanying funds transfers); Code de commerce Articles L.227-1 et seq. (SAS constitutional rules); ACPR General Regulation and the ACPR joint position of 14 June 2021 on the cartography of AML/CFT risks.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Registration / Certificate of Good Standing of the corporate shareholder (equivalent of a Kbis extract)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent commercial registry or chamber of commerce in the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (France is party to the Hague Convention of 5 October 1961)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the Articles of Association of the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or equivalent public officer in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney authorizing the incorporation of the French SAS and appointment of the local signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin or French notaire
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization where the origin state is not a party to the Apostille Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of the passport or national identity document of every ultimate beneficial owner and corporate signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public, civil registry or consular officer in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Tax residence certificate (certificat de résidence fiscale) of the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent tax authority of the shareholder's country of residence

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all UBOs, directors and authorized signatories against the French FCPI/FIUT list maintained by the Direction générale du Trésor, the EU consolidated financial sanctions list (in particular Regulation (EU) No 269/2014 and Regulation (EU) No 833/2014), and UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists; politically exposed persons (PEPs) must be identified under CMF Article L.561-10 and R.561-18, triggering enhanced due diligence, independent verification of source of wealth and source of funds, and senior management approval; because the target payment rails are milestone bank transfers and letters of credit, OFAC SDN-list screening is additionally applied by French partner banks as contractual policy for any USD-clearing chain, although it is not a standalone French statutory mandate.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises operated by the INPI at https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; national registry consultation via the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) at https://data.inpi.fr and the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via https://www.infogreffe.fr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The dénomination sociale must be expressed in Latin/Roman characters and may combine words, numerals and abbreviations (e.g., SAS); the constitutional documents and the mandatory public announcement in a Journal d'Annonces Légales must be in French; foreign-language names are admissible where written in Latin script and not misleading, but a French-language version is required for RNE indexing and to satisfy the commercial substance and publicity rules of Article L.123-1 of the Code de commerce; non-Latin scripts are rejected by the registry.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banking and financial terms requiring prior authorization from the ACPR or the competent ministry: 'Banque', 'Crédit', 'Finance', 'Assurance', 'Mutuelle'

Regulated professional titles reserved to holders of a protected qualification and registration: 'Avocat', 'Notaire', 'Huissier de justice', 'Commissaire de justice', 'Architecte', 'Médecin', 'Pharmacien'
Terms falsely implying a public authority or official status: 'National', 'Officiel', 'Chambre', 'État', 'Ministère'
Deceptive terms regarding the corporate object, including 'Géotechnicien agréé' or 'Ingénieur agréé' where the corresponding Qualibat certification is not held
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not operate a true statutory name-reservation register; the 30-day window denotes the de facto period within which preliminary availability screening at the RNE/infogreffe must be finalized through signature of the definitive Articles of Association. If the proposed dénomination sociale is rejected by the registrar during admissibility review at the Guichet Unique for lack of distinctiveness or risk of confusion with a prior registered name or trademark, the applicant may (i) submit a corrected name through a fresh electronic filing at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr without an additional publication penalty where no legal announcement has yet been published; or (ii) file an administrative appeal with the competent Tribunal judiciaire or Tribunal de commerce within two months of the refusal notice (a recours gracieux to the INPI being permitted before judicial recourse), supported by evidence of prior use, trademark registration or acquired distinctiveness; upon definitive annulment of the refusal, the registrar must complete the registration.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permissible: the SAS may validly use an approved domiciliation service (domiciliation agréée) for its registered office under Code de commerce Article L.123-11-1 and Law No. 94-126 of 11 February 1994, subject to a written one-year renewable contract and annual communication of the registered office address to the registry. However, for a geotechnical foundation and diaphragm wall contractor subject to compulsory decennial liability insurance (garantie décennale under Article L.241-1 of the Code de la construction et de l'habitation), a virtual office alone is insufficient to satisfy the commercial-substance and effective-management tests — a physical operational base or active French project site with technical equipment and qualified personnel is required for licensing and tax residency under Article 209 of the Code général des impôts.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High: unannounced on-site inspections are frequent for deep-foundation and groundworks operations — principally by the Inspection du travail under the Code du travail and by the DREAL under the Code de l'environnement (dangerous-site and groundwater-protection controls); estimated 70–80% probability of at least one unannounced physical inspection within the first 12 months of active contracting, plus routine desk audits of the registered office by the tax administration within the ordinary three-year audit window.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Independent French avocat registered at the regional Barreau
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for an international SAS incorporation with non-resident UBOs (EUR 2,100–EUR 2,900 range)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Mandatory publication of the incorporation notice in a Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL) for the SAS
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff for the legal announcement based on company name, registered office and duration (approx. EUR 180–EUR 230)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Incorporation filing fee at the Guichet Unique / Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (RNE registration and Kbis issuance)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI (Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle) via the Guichet Unique, with allocation to the Greffe
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated statutory tariff for creation of a SAS with capital below EUR 1,000,000 (approx. EUR 73.91 plus EUR 10.02 fixed procedural levy)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO (bénéficiaires effectifs) declaration preparation and filing for the Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of EUR 60–EUR 120 per page for sworn translations (estimated 2–3 pages plus certification)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarized power of attorney for remote incorporation of the SAS by non-resident shareholders
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Réglemented notarial tariff for the acte plus authentication formalities (approx. EUR 270–EUR 320)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for conflict search against registered company names and INPI trademarks (EUR 120–EUR 170)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP, sanctions and AML/UBO compliance file preparation (KYC pack for the French partner bank supporting milestone transfers and letters of credit)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for preparation of the encrypted compliance dossier required for account opening and payment-rail setup (EUR 150–EUR 220)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.210-1 to L.210-10 (general company law), L.227-1 to L.227-4 (Société par Actions Simplifiée), L.123-1 (registration), R.123-101 et seq. (registry procedure), and Code de l'environnement, R.122-2 for environmental screening where applicable.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce (Registry of the Commercial Court) in the jurisdiction of the registered office, acting via the Guichet unique operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration de constitution d'une société (single declaration unique via the Guichet unique electronique, formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an SAS; capital is freely set in the Articles, often €1. Cash contributions must be effectively paid and deposited in a blocked account with a bank, notary, or the Caisse des Dépôts before registration; at least 50% of cash contributions is released upon incorporation, and the balance shall be paid into the company's account within five years. Non-cash (in-kind) contributions are vested at once and must be fully described in the Articles.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That this SAS is incorporated under French law per the Articles of Association executed this day. FIRST: The share capital shown in the Articles is subscribed in full by the undersigned shareholders; the capital deposit certificate of the depositary bank is accepted and annexed. SECOND: The registered office is fixed at the address stated in the Articles; the Company is authorized to complete all registrations and administrative formalities there. THIRD: The President and other officers named in the Articles are appointed with full authority to represent the Company within legal limits and to execute all necessary filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and execute the Articles of Association of the SAS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate counsel and, where the contribution includes real property, a notaire; the final dossier is subsequently lodged through the Guichet unique.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the statutory articles in accordance with Articles L.227-1 to L.227-4 of the French Commercial Code. The articles must contain the company form (SAS), corporate name, registered office, corporate purpose covering ISIC 4390 deep foundation and diaphragm wall works, duration of up to 99 years, share capital with subdivision and class rights, rules for transfer of shares, appointment and dismissal of the President and supervisory officers, and decision-making procedures. Ensure each founder signs every original and each signature is authenticated; execute by electronic signature where permitted.
required_dossiers: Signed Articles of Association (original or electronic original)
Identity documents of founding shareholders (passport or national ID)
Justification of registered office (lease, ownership title, or domiciliation agreement)
Declaration of non-conviction (declaration de non-condamnation) for officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry rejects the articles for omission or ambiguity, prepare a rectification deed (document rectificatif) signed by all shareholders and refile. If a real-property contribution is unsupported by a notarial deed, have the notaire re-certify before refiling.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit and block the cash share capital with an authorized depositary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A French licensed bank, a notary, or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked account under the name of the company in formation. Transfer the total cash subscription amount into that account, complying with KYC/AML instructions. Obtain from the depositary the certificate of blocked capital (attestation de blocage de fonds / certificat de dépôt des fonds), which must state the company name, the account holder, the amount deposited and the date. The certificate will later be annexed to the registration filing.
required_dossiers: Completed bank account opening application for the company in formation
Draft Articles of Association
Identity documents of shareholders and appointed officers
Beneficial owner self-declaration if required by French AML rules
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank insists on enhanced due diligence, submit a correct beneficial-owner declaration and director identity documentation. If the depositary refuses on AML grounds, select another French bank or notary. If the certificate has a clerical error, request immediate reissue from the depositary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish the legal notice in an approved legal gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A publication outlet authorized to receive legal announcements (journal d'annonces légales) in the department of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the annonce légale containing the company’s legal form, name, registered office address, corporate object, share capital, duration, and the names of the officers. Submit the announcement to an approved legal gazette in the registered-office department. Pay all applicable publication fees and obtain the certificate of publication (attestation de parution). The certificate is a mandatory exhibit in the incorporation filing.
required_dossiers: Company name and legal form (SAS)
Registered office address and RCS filing city
Share capital amount and breakdown of cash and in-kind contributions
Full names and birth data of the President and officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the legal notice contains inaccurate data, publish a corrective notice in the same gazette and include both the original and the rectificatif in the registration file. If the publication does not appear within the prescribed deadline, republish and submit a new certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the registration dossier with the Commercial Court Registry via the Guichet unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet unique electronique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), managed by INPI and transmitted to the Greffe du tribunal de commerce of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the Guichet unique portal and complete the single declaration (déclaration unique) for company constitution. Select SAS and fill in the corporate data, share capital, registered office, shareholders, and officers. Attach the Articles of Association, legal notice certificate, capital deposit certificate, officer declarations, and, if filing by proxy, the power of attorney. Electronically pay the official filing fee and related taxes. The Registry will review the dossier and may request supplemental documents before issuing a final registration decision.
required_dossiers: Executed Articles of Association
Certificate of publication in a legal gazette (attestation de parution)
Certificate of deposit of the cash capital (attestation de blocage de fonds)
Identity and proof of address of each officer and shareholder
Declaration of no criminal conviction for officers
Declaration of beneficial owner where applicable
Power of attorney if filing is done by a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a notice of rejection or requests additional information, cure the deficiencies within 15 to 30 days by uploading supplementary documents through the same portal. Substantive errors in the articles must be corrected by a signed rectification deed. Failure to cure results in a final rejection and a fresh filing with a new fee, but minor omissions do not invalidate the incorporation if timely corrected.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receive the Kbis extract and complete post-registration formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce in the jurisdiction of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After successful vetting, the Registry issues the Kbis extract, which is the official proof of incorporation for the SAS. The Kbis includes the SIREN, SIRET, RCS number, legal form, registered office, officers, and principal activity NAF code matching the deep foundation and diaphragm wall business. Simultaneously, the company is entered into the RCS and its existence is legally effective. Use the Kbis to open the final permanent bank account, obtain a corporate seal, and notify clients, insurers, and the local Chamber of Commerce.
required_dossiers: Registry acceptance receipt or notification of completed registration
Kbis extract (generated by the Registry)
Coded NAF activity (to align with ISIC 4390)
Bank account confirmation and professional insurance certificates where relevant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Kbis contains an error (name, capital, or officer designation), file a rectification request with the Greffe within one month accompanied by the correct documents. If the Kbis is not issued after the stated SLA, verify the filing in the Guichet unique and contact the Registry directly; any missing document must be supplied or re-confirmed in writing.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement (DREAL) and the Inspection des installations classées (ICPE) under the French Ministry of Ecological Transition and Territorial Cohesion.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Déclaration, enregistrement, ou autorisation au titre des Installations Classées pour la Protection de l'Environnement (ICPE) for on-site concrete batching (Rubrique 2515) and fuel storage (Rubrique 4725); where applicable, a standalone operating permit under the Code de l'environnement.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement (DREAL) and, for national projects, the French General Council for Ecology and Sustainable Development.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Subject to case-by-case environmental examination (examen au cas par cas) under Article R.122-2 of the French Environmental Code. A full EIA report is required only if the works are within the thresholds of Annex II of the EIA Directive as transposed (e.g. excavation, water abstraction, or development of a concrete plant with a capacity above the registration thresholds). For most foundation works that remain temporary and below ICPE authorization thresholds, the company files an environmental registration or a prior declaration rather than a full EIA.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Discharges of pumped excavation water and bentonite slurry must meet the French water quality standards: suspended solids ≤ 35 mg/L, pH within 6.5–8.5, and no unpermitted release into surface or groundwater. Dust and VOC emissions from concrete plants and fuel storage must comply with the ministerial orders governing ICPE Rubriques 2515 and 4725. Waste concrete, slurry, and sludge must be characterized, disposed of or recycled through registered waste centers, and present proof of disposal records (traçabilité).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: obtain a fire safety certificate (certificat de sécurité) for site offices and any enclosed premises, with adequate extinguishing equipment and evacuation plans. Structural clearance: ensure the design, inspection, and testing of temporary works, sheet piles, diaphragm wall guides, cranes, and shoring comply with the Eurocodes and the employer's safety dossier (plan de prévention). Occupational clearance: all workers assigned to deep foundation operations must pass pre-employment medical examination through the service de santé au travail, and the firm must register with the French construction prevention or OPPBTP where applicable.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP), through the official impots.gouv.fr portal and the competent Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE). VAT registration and filings for non-established businesses are handled by the designated non-resident business tax service. Customs matters are administered separately by the Direction générale des douanes et droits indirects (DGDDI), including through douane.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Before commencing taxable activity in France, submit the applicable business-registration formalities through the Guichet unique operated by INPI and request VAT registration from the competent SIE. A French-established SAS receives a SIREN and establishment SIRET through the registration process; its French VAT number generally takes the form FR plus a two-character key and the SIREN. A foreign entity without a French establishment applies directly to the competent non-resident VAT service, supplying its incorporation and tax-residence evidence, business activities, identification details, and anticipated French transactions. An EU-established applicant may generally register directly. A non-EU applicant generally must appoint a French fiscal representative, subject to applicable mutual-assistance exceptions. A VAT number is required before making transactions for which French VAT registration is mandatory. Registration does not itself determine whether a permanent establishment or corporate-tax filing obligation exists.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A French SAS is ordinarily subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, or IS); there is no general US-style check-the-box election. A qualifying newly formed SAS may elect temporary taxation under the income-tax regime (impôt sur le revenu, or IR) for up to five financial years if statutory ownership, activity, age, and size conditions are met. The election is subject to deadlines and is not available solely by choice to every SAS. No general hybrid-mismatch classification election replaces the statutory French classification; anti-hybrid rules may deny deductions or impose inclusion under applicable French and EU law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT, taxe sur la valeur ajoutée or TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold protects a non-established business from French VAT registration where it makes taxable supplies in France for which it is liable to account for VAT. French small-business franchise thresholds apply only where their statutory conditions are met; they are not a general registration safe harbor for a foreign contractor. Construction and installation transactions may be subject to specific place-of-supply, invoicing, and domestic reverse-charge rules depending on the parties and transaction. Confirm the current threshold and treatment for the relevant tax period before relying on a small-business exemption.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing mandatory domestic B2B electronic invoicing and transaction/payment e-reporting through approved platforms connected to the DGFiP system. All businesses within scope must be able to receive e-invoices from 1 September 2026; issuance obligations are phased, with large and medium-sized businesses from 1 September 2026 and smaller businesses from 1 September 2027, subject to current statutory implementation rules. The regime is not a general requirement for real-time pre-clearance or digital stamping of every invoice. Required formats, platform transmission, and e-reporting depend on transaction type. Cross-border and certain consumer transactions generally fall under e-reporting rather than the domestic B2B e-invoice issuance obligation. Verify implementation dates and technical specifications before deployment.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods dispatched or transported from France to a destination outside the European Union may qualify for VAT exemption with a right to deduct (commonly described as zero-rating) when statutory export conditions are satisfied and the supplier retains reliable evidence of export. Intra-EU supplies are governed by separate exemption conditions, including valid customer VAT identification and evidence of transport. Services are not zero-rated merely because the customer or payment is offshore: the place-of-supply rules determine whether French VAT applies. B2B services supplied to a taxable customer established outside France are often outside the French VAT scope under the general rule, subject to exceptions; services directly connected with French immovable property, including relevant construction work, are generally located where the property is situated. A deep-foundation or diaphragm-wall contract performed on French land therefore requires transaction-specific analysis and ordinarily is not an export of services solely because the customer is non-resident.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration and MRN or other official evidence that the goods exited the EU customs territory
Commercial invoice identifying the supplier, customer, goods, VAT treatment, and transaction
Transport evidence appropriate to the route, such as bill of lading, airway bill, CMR consignment note, or carrier confirmation
Purchase order, contract, packing list, and proof of delivery or receipt where relevant
For services, contract, work descriptions, customer business-status evidence, place-of-supply analysis, and evidence supporting any claimed exemption or outside-scope treatment
Bank payment and remittance evidence where relevant to substantiating the transaction; France does not generally require an inward remittance certificate as a condition of export VAT exemption
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France does not impose a general statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export proceeds. A zero-rating or exemption claim unsupported by the required conditions and evidence may be denied, with assessed VAT, late-payment interest, and tax penalties. Deliberate fraud or false documentation can trigger enhanced tax penalties and, where applicable, criminal prosecution. Input VAT refunds may be adjusted or recovered if the underlying transactions do not qualify or supporting records are inadequate. Retain invoices, customs and transport records, contracts, accounting records, and VAT returns for the applicable statutory period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France maintains a liberalized capital account regime fully aligned with EU capital movement directives. Current account transactions are freely convertible at market rates. Capital account transactions including profit remittances and capital injections require no prior approval but are subject to mandatory reporting thresholds and enhanced AML/KYC verification. Profit remittance hurdles are limited to standard tax clearance, beneficial ownership documentation, and Banque de France statistical reporting obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender or conversion of export proceeds required under French law. Export receipts may be retained in foreign currency. Transactions exceeding €100,000 must be reported to the Banque de France via the SIE electronic reporting system for statistical purposes. Conversion to EUR occurs at prevailing market rates without statutory fixed ratios or surrender requirements.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for regulated fintech EMI providers including Revolut Business and Wise, subject to French AML regulations, AMF licensing requirements under the Payment Services Directive, and mandatory local banking partner arrangements for full correspondent clearing services.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote digital onboarding via e-KYC and video identification is permitted for standard corporate clients. Physical presence and in-person KYC interviews are required only for complex beneficial ownership structures, high-risk sectors, or when enhanced due diligence thresholds are triggered.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions exposure or adverse media screening
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening report, adverse media clearance certificate, and beneficial ownership declaration
Source of wealth documentation, relationship explanation, and senior management approval

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent beneficial ownership or shell company indicators
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate registry extract, shareholding agreement, and independent verification of control

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing via SWIFT MT103 messages with purpose code 'CAP' or 'EQTY'. Verification requires Banque de France reporting form, company incorporation documents, beneficial ownership certificate, and source of funds evidence. All transactions must comply with French foreign exchange reporting thresholds and AML screening protocols.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing via SWIFT MT103 for direct payments or issuance of Commercial Letters of Credit through correspondent banks. Trade settlements require presentation of shipping documents, invoices, contract proof, and compliance verification with anti-money laundering and export control regulations.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% corporate income tax. A 3.3% social contribution on corporate income tax may apply to companies with annual turnover of at least EUR 7.63 million and corporate income tax exceeding EUR 763,000, producing a maximum combined effective rate of approximately 25.83%. A reduced 15% rate may apply to qualifying small and medium-sized companies on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, subject to ownership, turnover, paid-in-capital, and capital-payment conditions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: France generally provides no general corporate tax holiday. Available incentives may include the 15% SME rate on qualifying profit, the research tax credit, certain innovation incentives, accelerated depreciation or investment incentives, regional aid, and tax credits applicable to specified activities. Incentive eligibility must be verified against the relevant statutory conditions, state-aid limits, substance requirements, and filing forms. The 25% rate remains the ordinary rate for a French SAS.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD for the corporate income tax return, filed electronically through the French tax administration professional portal or by EDI-TDFC through an authorized transmission provider. The return is accompanied by the applicable balance-sheet, income-statement, tax-reconciliation, and transfer-pricing schedules, principally Forms 2050-SD to 2059-G-SD or the simplified package Forms 2033-A-SD to 2033-G-SD.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a financial year ending on 31 December, the corporate income tax return is generally due by the second business day following 1 May of the following year, subject to the electronic filing timetable and any officially published filing tolerance. For a year-end other than 31 December, the return is generally due within three months after the end of the relevant financial year. A French SAS must also file its annual accounts with the competent registry within the statutory corporate-law deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, registered office, SIREN number, tax identification details, financial year dates, principal activity, and filing status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder is not entered as the taxpayer unless it operates a French permanent establishment. Report the French SAS as the taxpayer and identify the French establishment, branch, or fixed business location where applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit or tax loss calculated from the statutory accounts after French tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only income and deductible expenditure attributable to the French SAS or French permanent establishment. Apply French permanent-establishment attribution principles and exclude unsupported head-office allocations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation from accounting profit or loss to taxable profit or loss, including permanent add-backs, non-deductible expenses, exempt income, timing differences, and tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disallow expenses lacking business purpose, documentation, arm's-length support, or French deductibility. Related-party service, financing, royalty, and management charges require contemporaneous support.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Use of carried-forward tax losses and computation of the remaining tax-loss balance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply French loss-utilization limitations. Loss carryforward is generally unlimited in duration but subject to an annual utilization cap of EUR 1 million plus 50% of taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million; loss carryback is generally limited to the immediately preceding accounting period and subject to statutory caps.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, reductions, foreign tax credits, and other amounts reducing corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim foreign tax credits only where permitted by the applicable tax treaty or French domestic law and retain foreign tax certificates, payment evidence, and income attribution schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: 2059-A-SD to 2059-G-SD, capital gains and special computations
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of capital gains, depreciable assets, provisions, participation-related items, and specialized tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report disposals of French business assets, construction equipment, land, buildings, and participations according to the applicable French rules. Analyze treaty allocation before claiming exemption for non-resident shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: 2065-SD, corporate income tax and social contribution
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax liability, applicable reduced-rate computation, social contribution, tax credits, installments, and balance payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not apply treaty relief to the SAS's domestic corporate income tax unless a specific treaty provision and domestic mechanism apply. Treaty relief generally concerns cross-border withholding, not the French company's ordinary corporate tax base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Four corporate income tax installments generally payable on or around 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December, subject to statutory exceptions and payment thresholds.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The French SAS remains responsible for installments even where its shareholder is non-resident. Estimate current-year liability and adjust the final installment to prevent material underpayment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final corporate income tax balance after crediting installments, generally due by the filing deadline for the annual return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the balance to Form 2065-SD, filed accounts, tax credits, withholding credits, and payment confirmations. Maintain evidence of bank settlement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual summary of transactions with associated enterprises where the statutory filing thresholds and conditions are met.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose cross-border related-party transactions involving the non-resident shareholder, group companies, lenders, licensors, procurement entities, and service providers. Ensure consistency with the Local File, Master File, and accounting ledger.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer-pricing documentation and, where applicable, country-by-country reporting notification or reporting obligations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify the ultimate parent, reporting entity, jurisdictions, transaction categories, amounts, pricing methods, and documentation status. Do not use a generic group policy without French functional and economic analysis.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or omitted filing may trigger a 10% surcharge, increased to 40% in cases of deliberate non-compliance and potentially 80% in cases involving fraudulent maneuvers or abusive conduct. Late payment generally attracts a 5% surcharge and late-payment interest at 0.20% per month, subject to statutory rules and exceptions. Inaccurate returns may trigger reassessment, interest, penalties, denial of deductions, and criminal referral where fraud is suspected.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2571-SD for corporate income tax installments and Form 2572-SD for the final balance, filed and paid electronically through the French tax administration professional portal or through approved electronic payment channels.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Installments are generally payable on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December. The final balance is generally payable by the date applicable to the annual corporate income tax return. The exact due date may vary where the accounting year does not end on 31 December or where statutory payment exceptions apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SIREN, legal name, relevant financial year, and tax account information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the French SAS's SIREN and tax account details. A non-resident parent does not replace the French SAS as the installment taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Current-year or prior-year corporate income tax basis used to calculate the installment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude distributions to shareholders from the corporate tax installment base. Include taxable French operating profits and other French-source taxable income of the SAS.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, previous installments, and other offsets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only documented and legally available credits. Reconcile every offset to the annual return and retain supporting certificates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final corporate income tax, social contribution where applicable, installments paid, credits, and amount payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the final payment to the filed annual return and financial statements. A refund claim must identify the legal basis and provide bank and tax-account information.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment may generate a 5% surcharge and late-payment interest generally calculated at 0.20% per month. Underpayments may lead to additional interest and penalties after assessment. Persistent non-payment can result in enforced collection, bank-account attachment, seizure of assets, director liability proceedings in exceptional cases, and criminal tax-fraud exposure where concealment or fraudulent organization is established.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: The ordinary French withholding tax rate on dividends paid to non-resident recipients is generally 25%, subject to domestic exemptions, EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive implementation, tax treaties, and anti-abuse rules. Dividends paid to entities located in or connected with a French non-cooperative state or territory may be subject to a 75% rate unless a statutory exception applies. A qualifying EU or European Economic Area corporate parent may obtain exemption where the ownership, holding-period, subject-to-tax, beneficial-ownership, anti-abuse, and documentation conditions are satisfied.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The French paying entity should obtain a valid certificate of tax residence from the recipient's tax authority, verify beneficial ownership and treaty entitlement, test limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose anti-abuse rules where relevant, and retain ownership, holding-period, legal-form, subject-to-tax, and payment records. French treaty forms generally include Form 5000-FR and the relevant dividend, interest, or royalty annex, commonly Form 5001, 5002, or 5003 depending on the income category and relief mechanism. The applicable treaty rate may be applied at source where procedural requirements are met; otherwise the statutory withholding may be paid and a refund requested from the French tax administration. A treaty does not eliminate French withholding where the recipient lacks beneficial ownership, the arrangement is abusive, or anti-conduit rules apply.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: French-source royalties paid to non-residents are generally subject to a domestic withholding rate of 25%, with a possible 75% rate for payments to non-cooperative states or territories, subject to statutory exceptions. Tax treaties commonly reduce royalty withholding to rates ranging from 0% to 15%, depending on the treaty and beneficial ownership. Interest paid to non-residents is generally not subject to ordinary French withholding tax, but special rules apply to payments to non-cooperative states or territories, certain structured or connected-party arrangements, and payments recharacterized as distributions. Treaty interest rates commonly range from 0% to 15%. Interest deductibility is separately subject to French thin-capitalization, earnings-stripping, anti-hybrid, beneficial-ownership, and arm's-length rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory full transfer-pricing documentation generally applies where the French entity or French tax group has annual pre-tax turnover or gross assets of at least EUR 400 million, or where specified ownership or control links exist with an entity meeting the EUR 400 million threshold. The documentation obligation can also arise under other statutory conditions, including membership in a qualifying group. A transfer-pricing declaration and summary may apply at lower thresholds or under separate conditions. The Local File and Master File should be maintained contemporaneously and supplied within the statutory response period during an audit.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not operate a separate general-purpose Economic Substance Regulations regime equivalent to some offshore jurisdictions. French anti-abuse, beneficial-ownership, principal-purpose, abuse-of-law, controlled-foreign-company, anti-hybrid, interest-limitation, and permanent-establishment rules nevertheless require genuine commercial substance. The SAS should maintain French decision-making, personnel or operational capacity proportionate to its business, premises or effective operating arrangements, bank and accounting records, contract-performance evidence, construction-site documentation, asset ownership or control, and commercial risk assumption. Conduit companies, circular financing, artificial royalty chains, non-arm's-length management charges, and arrangements lacking business purpose may be denied treaty benefits or deductions and may trigger reassessment and penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional omission of revenue, fictitious invoices, concealed cash receipts, false subcontractor costs, duplicate accounting, undeclared permanent-establishment activity, or deliberate understatement of taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, late-payment interest, penalties generally up to 80% for fraudulent maneuvers, and criminal tax-fraud penalties that may include imprisonment and substantial fines. Aggravated fraud involving organized concealment, offshore structures, or false documentation may attract enhanced criminal sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may incur criminal liability, civil restitution, tax-liability proceedings for fraudulent or seriously negligent conduct, management bans, and asset-seizure measures. Imprisonment is fact-dependent and not automatic. A general travel ban is not a standard tax penalty, but judicial restrictions may arise in criminal proceedings or from immigration and enforcement measures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company, Artificial Interposition, or Treaty Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the SAS as a conduit with no genuine French activity, passing dividends, royalties, or interest to an ultimate recipient while falsely claiming treaty or EU relief, or creating artificial subcontracting and management chains.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, withholding-tax reassessment, disallowance of deductions, abuse-of-law penalties generally up to 80% where the statutory conditions are met, late-payment interest, and possible criminal referral for fraudulent documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal civil liability for intentional or gross misconduct, criminal liability for participation in fraud, management bans, and restitution of improperly avoided tax. Corporate personality does not protect a director from personal liability for their own unlawful conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Inflated related-party service fees, unsupported royalty payments, excessive shareholder debt, non-arm's-length interest, unpriced use of equipment, profit shifting from French construction operations, or inconsistent Local File and financial-ledger data.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary transfer-pricing adjustment, withholding-tax exposure, denial of deductions, interest limitation, penalties for incomplete or missing documentation, and possible 40% or 80% penalties where deliberate or fraudulent conduct is established.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable where they knowingly approved false documentation, abusive payments, or diversion of corporate assets. Criminal liability requires proof of the relevant offense and personal participation or complicity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Performing deep foundation, diaphragm-wall, or other construction works in France through a foreign entity while omitting a French permanent establishment, splitting contracts or site periods artificially, or using personnel and equipment without proper French registration and tax reporting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: French corporate income tax and business-tax reassessment, payroll and social-security exposure, VAT reassessment, withholding obligations, interest, penalties, and possible permanent-establishment anti-abuse findings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil liability, employment and social-security sanctions, and criminal exposure for deliberate concealment or false declarations. A travel ban or imprisonment is not automatic and depends on judicial findings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to charge, self-assess, or report French VAT; incorrect reverse-charge treatment; undeclared site activity; false subcontractor VAT invoices; or failure to preserve work certificates, progress bills, and customer documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT reassessment, late-payment interest, 5%, 10%, 40%, or 80% penalties depending on the conduct, invoice-related penalties, denial of input VAT, and potential criminal proceedings for organized VAT fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur personal liability for fraudulent VAT conduct or serious repeated non-compliance, including civil restitution, management bans, asset measures, and imprisonment where criminal liability is established.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained third-party payments, using opaque subcontractor chains, failing to identify beneficial owners, bypassing customer or supplier due diligence, or structuring milestone and letter-of-credit payments to conceal the source or destination of funds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Regulatory sanctions, transaction blocking, suspicious-transaction reporting consequences, professional or licensing restrictions, confiscation, fines, and criminal money-laundering penalties where the underlying conduct is proven.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for knowing participation, facilitation, or negligent governance where a statutory duty is breached. Criminal sanctions can include imprisonment and fines; travel restrictions may arise only through judicial measures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Bribes, secret commissions, facilitation payments, bid manipulation, undisclosed intermediary commissions, falsified work-completion certificates, or payments to public officials or politically exposed persons in connection with infrastructure works.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fines, imprisonment, confiscation, exclusion from public procurement, contract termination, damages, and corporate compliance-monitoring measures. Accounting entries for bribes are non-deductible.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, employees, intermediaries, and beneficial owners may be prosecuted personally. Civil restitution, management bans, asset confiscation, judicial restrictions, and imprisonment may apply according to the offense and individual participation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Asset Diversion and Improper Profit Repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends without distributable profits, disguising dividends as loans or fees, paying shareholder expenses from company accounts, repaying fictitious debt, or transferring assets below market value.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of improper distributions, corporate and withholding-tax reassessment, denial of deductions, interest, penalties, and potential criminal liability for misuse of corporate assets or fraudulent bankruptcy conduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be required to restore diverted assets, compensate creditors, bear liability for insufficient assets in insolvency proceedings, and face management bans or imprisonment where the relevant criminal offense is proven.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False Corporate Records and Filing Misrepresentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Submitting materially false tax returns, fabricated transfer-pricing reports, forged certificates of residence, false shareholder records, inaccurate beneficial-owner declarations, or contradictory statutory accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative reassessment, filing penalties, document-forgery sanctions, corporate-law penalties, criminal fines, and imprisonment depending on the document and intent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The individual signatory and responsible officers may be prosecuted independently of the SAS. Personal civil damages, restitution, management bans, judicial restrictions, and imprisonment may apply where intentional falsification is established.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlicensed or Non-Compliant Regulated Construction Activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Carrying out regulated foundation, excavation, site, safety, environmental, or public-works activities without required registrations, insurance, technical qualifications, permits, or mandatory site controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative orders, work suspension, fines, contract cancellation, exclusion from public procurement, remediation costs, insurance denial, and criminal sanctions for serious safety or environmental violations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and site managers may face personal criminal and civil liability for workplace injury, environmental damage, fraudulent certification, or deliberate regulatory avoidance, including fines and imprisonment in serious cases.
